title: Randy: The Fumblers' Steady Climber, Still Chasing the Bowl and Still Not Taking Your Trade Offer
body: Some managers arrive with a splash. Randy arrived with a roster and an apparent vow never to let anyone else touch it. The fumblers opened Buckaroo history in 2023 at a perfectly balanced 7-7, scoring 1,462.9 points, grabbing the 3 seed and finishing third out of six. It was not flashy, but it was a playoff team in year one. That season also produced his career low, a 73.1-point dud against Kaushal in week 6 that he would probably rather we left out of the club history. We did not.

2024 was a step up in every number. The fumblers went 8-6, climbed to 1,595.1 points and earned the 2 seed, which sounds like a contender until you notice they finished fourth. The highlight was a 162.5-point explosion against Ramon in week 3, still the best week of Randy's career and a big reason he leads that head-to-head 7-4. The trade log for those first two seasons reads like a Bears receiving corps in a bad year: zero. Not one deal in 28 regular-season weeks, which has to be some kind of league record for a guy who complains this much about his roster.

Then came 2025, the best season of Randy's run so far. The fumblers went 9-7, piled up 1,792.1 points, took the 2 seed again and finally broke through for a playoff win to reach Buckaroo Bowl III. Waiting there was Sonny, finishing his worst-to-first redemption tour, and Randy settled for runner-up. He did make his first-ever trade that year, along with a career-high 16 pickups, so apparently it takes a title run to pry one deal loose. His career playoff record now sits at 1-3, the one number that keeps this page from having a trophy on it.

The rivalries tell the rest of the story. Alan has been Randy's real problem, holding a 8-5 edge that makes Team Pillbert the matchup he dreads most, and Sonny has the upper hand at 5-3 with a Bowl win on top. Randy owns Ramon at 7-4, edges Kaushal 6-5 and sits dead even with Mekhi at 6-6, about as fair a fight as this league has. He is also a perfect 1-0 against each of the 2026 newcomers, Jordan and Zoe, and you can bet the win over the Wisconsin rookie got mentioned in a Bears-vs-Packers argument or two.

Which brings us to 2026, where the fumblers sit at 3-4 with 752.4 points and title odds of just 3 percent. Randy has been busier than ever, with 14 pickups through seven weeks and another trade on the books, so the guy who once treated his roster like a vault is now working the phones like he means it. The scoring pace is right around last year's, so this is not a team falling apart so much as one waiting on a few breaks. Three straight playoff trips and an upward climb say do not count him out yet. Four seasons and zero rings say he knows exactly how long the wait can be.
